scenario: AITA for being uncomfortable when my boyfriend speaks Spanish to his family around me? | I’m very rarely with my boyfriend and his family, but the few times I have been, they’d only communicate with one another through Spanish, which is a language I hardly know at all. His whole family speaks English as well, but they choose to speak Spanish to one another around me, which makes me uncomfortable because a lot of times it’s regarding plans we’ve made and then my boyfriend has to turn to me and translate what they’ve all been saying, and often he leaves things out and forgets to tell me those necessary details until later. Now of course I don’t mind if it’s like, his siblings to his mother in a conversation that shouldn’t involve me, but when they’re talking with my boyfriend as he’s sitting right next to me, I just feel weird. I understand it’s their “normal language” as my boyfriend calls it, and I’m not trying to be all up in the business or try to have them change their ways, it just makes me feel left out and extremely confused and even a little awkward... I’ve mentioned it to him and he gets defensive and angry, like they’re not going to change to make me more comfortable. I just feel that if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend would understand so he wouldn’t feel left out or like he’s missing something important. Before anyone tells me to simply learn Spanish, first of all, it’s not that easy and second, I am learning Spanish...trying to at least... I feel like I AM the asshole but I don’t want to be...so someone just tell me, am I the asshole?

I’ve mentioned it to him and he gets defensive and angry, like they’re not going to change to make me more comfortable. I just feel that if the roles were reversed, I would have my family speak to me in a language my boyfriend would understand so he wouldn’t feel left out or like he’s missing something important. Before anyone tells me to simply learn Spanish, first of all, it’s not that easy and second, I am learning Spanish...trying to at least... I feel like I AM the asshole but I don’t want to be...so someone just tell me, am I the asshole?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw:
0. 

You're not the asshole in this situation. It's understandable that you feel left out and uncomfortable when your boyfriend's family speaks Spanish around you, especially when it involves plans or discussions that affect you. While it's great that you're making an effort to learn Spanish, it's not reasonable to expect you to become fluent overnight.

Your boyfriend's family choosing to speak Spanish exclusively around you, despite being able to speak English, can be seen as thoughtless or even rude. It's not about changing their "normal language" or expecting them to cater to you, but rather about being considerate of your feelings and including you in conversations that involve you.

Your analogy about reversing the roles is a good one. If the situation were reversed, it's likely that you would make an effort to include your boyfriend in conversations by speaking a language he understands. It's not too much to ask for the same courtesy from your boyfriend's family.

Your boyfriend's defensiveness and anger when you bring up the issue are not helpful and may indicate that he's not taking your feelings into account. It's essential to have an open and honest conversation with him about how you feel and find a compromise that works for everyone. Perhaps his family could make an effort to speak English when discussing plans or topics that involve you, or your boyfriend could make a greater effort to keep you informed and included in the conversation.
